contents.html: Note: This includes the following:
contents.html_ja: 注：これには次のものが含まれます。

contents.html: The project is progressing toward achieving established security goals and objectives.
contents.html_ja: プロジェクトが、確立されたセキュリティ上の到達目標と目的の達成に向けて進捗しています。

contents.html: The project is complying with project security directives.
contents.html_ja: プロジェクトが、プロジェクトのセキュリティ指令を遵守しています。

contents.html: The project is being conducted according to the security aspects of project life cycle policies, processes, and procedures.
contents.html_ja: プロジェクトが、プロジェクトのライフサイクルの方針、プロセス、および手順のセキュリティ面に従って遂行されています。

contents.html: The project remains viable, as indicated by the continuing need for security services, practical secure product implementation, and acceptable security-driven investment benefits.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティサービスに対する継続的なニーズ、実用的なセキュア製品の実装、および許容可能なセキュリティ主導の投資便益が示すとおり、プロジェクトが引き続き実行可能です。

contents.html: PM-2.2 Act to continue projects that are satisfactorily progressing in consideration of project security aspects.
contents.html_ja: PM-2.2 プロジェクトのセキュリティ面を考慮して、満足に進捗しているプロジェクトを継続する措置をとります。

contents.html: PM-2.3 Act to redirect projects that can be expected to progress satisfactorily with appropriate security-informed redirection.
contents.html_ja: PM-2.3 セキュリティを踏まえた適切な方向転換によって満足に進捗すると見込めるプロジェクトを、方向転換する措置をとります。

contents.html: AQ-1.1 Define the security aspects of the strategy for how the acquisition will be conducted.
contents.html_ja: AQ-1.1 調達の実施方法に関する戦略のセキュリティ側面を定義します。

contents.html: Note: This strategy describes or references the life cycle model, security risks and issues mitigation, a schedule of security-relevant milestones, the protection of acquirer and supplier assets, and security-relevant selection criteria if the supplier is external to the acquiring organization. It also includes key security drivers and security-relevant characteristics of the acquisition, such as responsibilities and liabilities; specific models, methods, or processes; formality; level of criticality; and the priority of security within relevant trade-off factors.
contents.html_ja: 注：この戦略では、ライフサイクルモデル、セキュリティリスクおよび問題の緩和、セキュリティ関連マイルストーンのスケジュール、取得者および供給者の資産の保護、ならびに供給者が取得組織の外部にある場合のセキュリティ関連選定基準を記述または参照します。また、責任および責任負担、特定のモデル・方法・プロセス、形式性、重要度、関連するトレードオフ要因におけるセキュリティの優先度など、調達に関する主要なセキュリティ推進要因およびセキュリティ関連特性も含みます。

contents.html: Note: The request includes security criteria for the business practices with which the supplier is to comply, a list of bidders with adequate security qualifications, and the security criteria that will be used to select the supplier.

contents.html: Note: This agreement can range in formality. Appropriate to the level of formality, the agreement establishes security requirements, secure development and delivery milestones, security verification, security validation, and the security aspects of acceptance conditions, process requirements (e.g., configuration management, risk management, and measurement), and the handling of data rights and intellectual property. rebuilt_blocks.html: Systems security engineering provides complementary engineering capabilities that extend the concept of trustworthiness to deliver trustworthy secure systems. Trustworthiness is not only about demonstrably meeting a set of requirements. The requirements must also be complete, consistent, and correct. From a security perspective, a trustworthy system meets a set of well-defined requirements, including security requirements. Through evidence and expert judgment, trustworthy secure systems can limit and prevent the effects of modern adversities. Such adversities come in malicious and non-malicious forms and can emanate from a variety of sources, including physical and electronic. Adversities can include attacks from determined and capable adversaries, human errors of omission and commission, accidents and incidents, component faults and failures, abuses and misuses, and natural and human-made disasters.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: システムセキュリティエンジニアリングは、信頼性の概念を拡張し、信頼できるセキュアシステムを実現するための相補的なエンジニアリング能力を提供する。信頼性は、一連の要求事項を実証可能な形で満たすことだけではない。要求事項は完全、一貫かつ正確でなければなりない。セキュリティの観点では、信頼できるシステムは、セキュリティ要求事項を含む明確に定義された要求事項を満たす。証拠と専門家の判断により、信頼できるセキュアシステムは現代の逆境の影響を抑制し、防止できる。逆境には悪意あるものとそうでないものがあり、物理的・電子的なものを含むさまざまな発生源から生じる。逆境には、意欲と能力を備えた敵対者による攻撃、人的な不作為・作為の誤り、事故やインシデント、コンポーネントの故障や不具合、乱用や誤用、自然災害および人為災害などがある。

rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: エンジニアリング主導の解決策

rebuilt_blocks.html: The effectiveness of any engineering discipline first requires a thorough understanding of the problem and consideration of all feasible solutions before acting to solve the identified problem. To maximize the effectiveness of systems security engineering, the security requirements for the protection against asset loss must be driven by business, mission, and all other stakeholder asset loss concerns. The security requirements are defined and managed as a well-defined set of engineering requirements and cannot be addressed independently or after the fact. In the context of systems security engineering, the term protection has a broad scope and is primarily focused on the concept of assets and asset loss resulting in unacceptable consequences. The protection capability provided by a system goes beyond prevention and aims to control the events, conditions, and consequences that constitute asset loss. It is achieved in the form of the specific capability and constraints on system architecture, design, function, implementation, construction, selection of technology, methods, and tools and must be “engineered in” as part of the system life cycle process.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: あらゆるエンジニアリング分野の有効性は、特定された問題を解決する行動に移る前に、問題を十分に理解し、実現可能なすべての解決策を検討することから始まる。システムセキュリティエンジニアリングの有効性を最大化するには、資産損失に対する保護のセキュリティ要求事項を、ビジネス、ミッションおよびその他すべてのステークホルダーの資産損失に関する懸念に基づいて定める必要がある。セキュリティ要求事項は、明確に定義された一連のエンジニアリング要求事項として定義・管理しなければならず、個別に、または事後に対処できるものではない。システムセキュリティエンジニアリングでいう保護は広い範囲を持ち、許容できない結果を伴う資産および資産損失の概念を主に対象とする。システムが提供する保護能力は、予防にとどまらず、資産損失を構成する事象、状態および結果の制御を目指す。具体的な能力と、システムアーキテクチャ、設計、機能、実装、構築、技術の選定、方法およびツールに関する制約として実現し、システムライフサイクルプロセスの一部として「設計に組み込む」必要がある。

The elements provide an asset-protection basis to determine the objectives for a secure system, optimize the system protection capability, and judge the overall suitability and effectiveness of the implemented protections.33 The elements are also grouped into two objectives to facilitate reasoning about the asset of interest:

rebuilt_blocks.html: The context of loss establishes the boundary, scope, and time frame for the reasoning, analyses, assessments, and conclusions about the asset of interest. The context of loss also provides a basis to relate and trace asset dependencies and interactions and to group assets for protection. The context of loss time frame is particularly important because the asset of interest has a life cycle35 that is different from the system of interest.36 For example, the asset of interest may be created, configured, or modified outside of the scope of control of the system of interest yet be within the scope of the engineering effort. The asset of interest, once within the scope of control of the system of interest, may have differing protection needs associated with the state or mode of the system (e.g., the system operational mode protection may differ from the system training mode). Additionally, system life cycle assets (Section 3.8) may only exist within a development or production system and their associated supporting environments. The effect of the loss for these assets may transfer to a loss associated with the system of interest. Therefore, the context of loss includes the life cycle of the asset, the state and mode of the system, and other time-based periods or characteristics during which loss is addressed.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 損失のコンテキストは、対象資産に関する推論、分析、評価および結論の境界、範囲、時間枠を定める。また、資産の依存関係と相互作用を関連付けて追跡し、資産を保護のためにグループ化する基礎にもなる。対象資産のライフサイクル³⁵は対象システムのライフサイクルと異なるため、損失の時間枠は特に重要である。³⁶ 例えば、対象資産は対象システムの制御範囲外で作成、設定または変更される一方、エンジニアリング作業の範囲内にある場合がある。対象資産が対象システムの制御範囲に入った後も、システムの状態・モードに応じて保護ニーズが異なる場合がある（運用モードと訓練モードでは必要な保護が異なるなど）。さらに、システムライフサイクル資産（3.8節）は、開発・生産システムとそれを支援する環境にのみ存在する場合がある。これらの資産の損失は、対象システムに関連する損失へ移行することがある。したがって損失のコンテキストには、資産のライフサイクル、システムの状態・モード、その他損失に対処する期間や特性が含まれる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Do not focus on what is likely to happen. Instead, focus on what can happen, and be prepared. That is what systems security engineering means by adopting a preemptive and reactive strategy (Section D.2) in the form of a concept of secure function that addresses the spectrum of asset loss and associated consequences. This means proactively planning and designing to prevent the loss of an asset that you are not willing to accept, to be able to minimize the consequences should such a loss occur, and to be in an informed position to reactively recover from the loss when it does happen.

Stakeholders are typically unaware of the existence of system assets and are not able to make decisions about the protection needs for system assets. The protection of system assets is an element of trustworthy secure system design.

rebuilt_blocks.html: Appendix B. Glossary
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 付録B. 用語集

rebuilt_blocks.html: abstraction View of an object that focuses on the information relevant to a particular purpose and ignores the remainder of the information. [24]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: abstraction（抽象化） 特定の目的に関連する情報に焦点を当て、その他の情報を無視するオブジェクトの見方。[24]

rebuilt_blocks.html: acquirer Stakeholder that acquires or procures a product or service from a supplier. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: acquirer（取得者） 供給者から製品またはサービスを取得もしくは調達する利害関係者。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: acquisition Process of obtaining a system, product, or service. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: acquisition（取得） システム、製品、またはサービスを取得するプロセス。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: activity Set of cohesive tasks of a process. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: activity（アクティビティ） プロセスを構成する、一貫性のあるタスクの集合。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: adequate security (systems) Meets minimum tolerable levels of security as determined by analysis, experience, or a combination of both and is as secure as reasonably practicable (i.e., incremental improvement in security would require an intolerable or disproportionate deterioration of meeting other system objectives, such as those for system performance, or would violate system constraints).
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: adequate security (systems)（適切なセキュリティ［システム］） 分析、経験、またはその両方によって定められた、許容可能な最低限のセキュリティ水準を満たし、合理的に実行可能な限りセキュアであること（すなわち、セキュリティを段階的に改善すると、システム性能などの他のシステム目的の達成が許容できないほど、または不釣り合いに損なわれるか、システム制約に違反することになる）。

rebuilt_blocks.html: adverse consequence An undesirable consequence associated with a loss. [61]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: adverse consequence（有害な結果） 損失に関連する望ましくない結果。[61]

rebuilt_blocks.html: adversity The conditions that can cause a loss of assets (e.g., threats, attacks, vulnerabilities, hazards, disruptions, and exposures).
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: adversity（逆境） 資産の損失を引き起こし得る状態（例えば、脅威、攻撃、脆弱性、危険、混乱、および曝露）。

rebuilt_blocks.html: agreement Mutual acknowledgement of terms and conditions under which a working relationship is conducted (e.g., memorandum of agreement or contract). [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: agreement（合意） 作業上の関係を遂行する際の条件についての相互確認（例えば、合意覚書または契約）。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: anomaly Condition that deviates from expectations based on requirements specifications, design documents, user documents, or standards, or from someone’s perceptions or experiences. [24]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: anomaly（異常） 要件仕様、設計文書、ユーザー文書、もしくは規格に基づく期待、または個人の認識や経験から逸脱する状態。[24]

rebuilt_blocks.html: anti-tamper Systems engineering activities intended to prevent or delay exploitation of critical program information in U.S. defense systems in domestic and export configurations to impede countermeasure development, unintended technology transfer, or alteration of a system due to reverse engineering. [70] See tampering.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: anti-tamper（耐改ざん） 米国の防衛システムの国内向けおよび輸出向け構成において、対抗策の開発、意図しない技術移転、またはリバースエンジニアリングによるシステムの改変を妨げるため、重要なプログラム情報の悪用を防止または遅延させることを目的としたシステムズエンジニアリング活動。[70] tamperingを参照。

rebuilt_blocks.html: architecture Fundamental concepts or properties related to a system in its environment embodied in its elements, relationships, and in the principles of its design and evolution. [71] See security architecture.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: architecture（アーキテクチャ） 環境内のシステムに関する基本概念または特性であり、その要素、関係、ならびに設計および進化の原則に具体化されたもの。[71] security architectureを参照。

rebuilt_blocks.html: architecture (system) Fundamental concepts or properties of a system in its environment embodied in its elements, relationships, and in the principles of its design and evolution. [71]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: architecture (system)（アーキテクチャ［システム］） 環境内のシステムの基本概念または特性であり、その要素、関係、ならびに設計および進化の原則に具体化されたもの。[71]

rebuilt_blocks.html: architecture description A work product used to express an architecture. [71]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: architecture description（アーキテクチャ記述） アーキテクチャを表現するために用いられる作業成果物。[71]

rebuilt_blocks.html: architecture framework Conventions, principles, and practices for the description of architectures established within a specific domain of application and/or community of stakeholders. [71] architecture view A work product expressing the architecture of a system from the perspective of specific system concerns. [71]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: architecture framework（アーキテクチャフレームワーク） 特定の適用領域および／または利害関係者コミュニティ内で確立された、アーキテクチャ記述のための規約、原則、および実践。[71] architecture view（アーキテクチャビュー） 特定のシステム上の関心事の視点からシステムアーキテクチャを表現する作業成果物。[71]

page_check.proof_note: joins the entry 'architecture framework' with the separate entry 'architecture view' (which is printed at the top of page 66); 'architecture framework' entry is printed on page 65; on this page only the separate entry 'architecture view' appears

rebuilt_blocks.html: architecture viewpoint A work product establishing the conventions for the construction, interpretation, and use of architecture views to frame specific system concerns. [71]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: architecture viewpoint（アーキテクチャビューポイント） 特定のシステム上の関心事を枠組み化するため、アーキテクチャビューの構築、解釈、および使用に関する規約を定める作業成果物。[71]

rebuilt_blocks.html: artifact Work products that are produced and used during a project to capture and convey information (e.g., models, source code). [72]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: artifact（成果物） 情報を記録し伝達するため、プロジェクト中に作成され使用される作業成果物（例えば、モデル、ソースコード）。[72]

rebuilt_blocks.html: aspect The parts, features, and characteristics used to describe, consider, interpret, or assess something.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: aspect（側面） 何かを記述、検討、解釈、または評価するために用いる部分、特徴、および特性。

rebuilt_blocks.html: asset Anything that has value to a person or organization. [24]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: asset（資産） 個人または組織にとって価値のあるもの。[24]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note 1: Assets have interrelated characteristics that include value, criticality, and the degree to which they are relied upon to achieve organizational mission and business objectives. From these characteristics, appropriate protections are to be engineered into solutions employed by the organization. Note 2: An asset may be tangible (e.g., physical item such as hardware, software, firmware, computing platform, network device, or other technology components) or intangible (e.g., information, data, trademark, copyright, patent, intellectual property, image, or reputation).
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注1：資産には、価値、重要度、ならびに組織のミッションおよび事業目的の達成にどの程度依存されているかを含む、相互に関連する特性がある。これらの特性に基づき、組織が採用するソリューションには適切な保護を設計し組み込まなければならない。注2：資産は有形（例えば、ハードウェア、ソフトウェア、ファームウェア、コンピューティングプラットフォーム、ネットワーク機器、その他の技術コンポーネントなどの物理的なもの）または無形（例えば、情報、データ、商標、著作権、特許、知的財産、イメージ、または評判）であり得る。

page_check.proof_note: joins Note 1 and Note 2, which are separate paragraphs

rebuilt_blocks.html: assurance Grounds for justified confidence that a claim has been or will be achieved. [61]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: assurance（保証） 主張が達成された、または達成されるという正当化された確信の根拠。[61]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note 1: Assurance is typically obtained relative to a set of specific claims. The scope and focus of such claims may vary (e.g., security claims, safety claims), and the claims themselves may be interrelated. Note 2: Assurance is obtained through techniques and methods that generate credible evidence to substantiate claims.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注1：保証は通常、特定の主張の集合に関して得られる。主張の範囲と焦点は異なり得る（例えば、セキュリティ主張、安全性主張）。また、主張自体が相互に関連する場合がある。注2：保証は、主張を裏付ける信頼性のある証拠を生成する技法および方法を通じて得られる。

page_check.proof_note: joins Note 1 and Note 2, which are separate paragraphs

rebuilt_blocks.html: assurance case A reasoned, auditable artifact created that supports the contention that its top-level claim (or set of claims) is satisfied, including systematic argumentation and its underlying evidence and explicit assumptions that support the claim(s). [61]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: assurance case（保証ケース） トップレベルの主張（または主張群）が満たされているという主張を裏付けるために作成される、論理的で監査可能な成果物。主張を支える体系的な論証、その基礎となる証拠、および明示的な前提を含む。[61]

rebuilt_blocks.html: assurance evidence The information upon which decisions regarding assurance, trustworthiness, and risk of the solution are substantiated.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: assurance evidence（保証の証拠） ソリューションの保証、信頼性、およびリスクに関する意思決定を裏付ける情報。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: Assurance evidence is specific to an agreed-upon set of claims. The security perspective focuses on assurance evidence for security-relevant claims, whereas other engineering disciplines may have their own focus (e.g., safety).
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：保証の証拠は、合意された特定の主張の集合に固有である。セキュリティの視点はセキュリティ関連の主張に関する保証の証拠に焦点を当てる一方、他のエンジニアリング分野はそれぞれ独自の焦点（例えば、安全性）を持つ場合がある。

rebuilt_blocks.html: This appendix discusses the approach and considerations for applying technical63 concepts of a trustworthy secure system design. The concepts described provide a balanced and integrated approach that optimally protects against asset loss. The discussions include the design approach for trustworthy systems (Section D.1), authorized and intended behaviors and outcomes of the system (Section D.2), security design order of precedence (Section D.3), and functional design and trade space considerations (Section D.4).
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 本付録では、信頼できるセキュアなシステム設計の技術的63概念を適用するためのアプローチおよび考慮事項を説明する。説明する概念は、資産損失に対して最適な保護を提供する、均衡の取れた統合的なアプローチをもたらす。内容には、信頼できるシステムの設計アプローチ（セクションD.1）、認可され意図されたシステムの振る舞いおよび結果（セクションD.2）、セキュリティ設計の優先順位（セクションD.3）、ならびに機能設計とトレードスペース上の考慮事項（セクションD.4）が含まれる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: TRUSTWORTHY SECURE DESIGN Trustworthy secure design is a means to provide stakeholders with the
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 信頼できるセキュアな設計 信頼できるセキュアな設計は、利害関係者に次の確信を与える手段である。

rebuilt_blocks.html: confidence that their conflicting capability needs, concerns, priorities, and constraints are satisfied.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 相反する能力ニーズ、懸念事項、優先事項、および制約が満たされている。

rebuilt_blocks.html: The design approach for engineering trustworthy secure systems is intended to establish and maintain the ability to deliver system capabilities at an acceptable level of performance64 while minimizing the occurrence and extent of loss. This approach provides a system structure for optimal employment of the engineered features and devices. The system design must provide the intended behaviors and outcomes, avoid the unintended behaviors and outcomes, prevent loss, and limit loss when it occurs. A trustworthy secure design includes a situational awareness capability and margin65 to account for adversity due to the unknowns and uncertainty inherent in the system and in its operational environment. The situational awareness capability helps to determine accountability for the actions of all users and entities (e.g., audit, logging, event recording) and detect pending and actual failure (e.g., by crossing the threshold of the margins that have been established). The design principle of Anomaly Detection embodies this capability.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 信頼できるセキュアなシステムを設計するためのアプローチは、損失の発生および規模を最小限に抑えながら、許容可能な性能水準64でシステム能力を提供する能力を確立し、維持することを目的とする。このアプローチは、設計された機能および装置を最適に活用するためのシステム構造を提供する。システム設計は、意図された振る舞いおよび結果を提供し、意図しない振る舞いおよび結果を回避し、損失を防止し、損失が発生した場合にはその損失を制限しなければならない。信頼できるセキュアな設計には、システムおよびその運用環境に本質的に存在する未知事項や不確実性に起因する逆境を考慮するため、状況認識能力とマージン65が含まれる。状況認識能力は、すべての利用者および実体の行動に対する説明責任を判定し（例えば、監査、ログ記録、事象記録）、差し迫った故障および実際の故障を検知するのに役立つ（例えば、設定されたマージンのしきい値を超えた場合）。異常検知の設計原則は、この能力を具現化する。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Some emergence is desired and productive; other emergence is not desired or productive, creating unknown, unforeseen, or adverse effects.68 Engineering trustworthy secure systems seeks to deliver only desired emergence. Trustworthiness judgments are based on the expectation that the system can satisfy the stated capability needs. rebuilt_blocks.html: The security design order of precedence (SecDOP)69 is a design approach with the objective of minimizing the system design basis for loss potential. SecDOP emphasizes the importance of establishing a secure structural context for the employment of engineered features and devices. Using a principled engineering approach, the SecDOP eliminates susceptibility, hazard, and vulnerability to the extent practicable, thereby eliminating the associated risk. For those cases in which susceptibility, hazard, or vulnerability cannot be eliminated, the SecDOP reduces the potential of experiencing a loss to an acceptable level within the constraints of cost, schedule, and performance. The SecDOP identifies design alternatives in order of decreasing effectiveness, thus enabling a maximized return on investment.

rebuilt_blocks.html: The principles for trustworthy secure design are representative of the practices of the safety, security, reliability, survivability, and resilience communities and the specialty engineering disciplines associated with those communities. Collectively, the goals of these practices represent the end objectives that the system must satisfy for trustworthy control of adverse effects. The principles are grounded in research, development, and application experience starting with the early incorporation of mechanisms into trusted operating systems to today’s components, environments, and systems and are expected to remain universally applicable for new, emerging, and maturing approaches. The concepts and theorems from the disciplines of computer science, computer engineering, systems engineering, control systems, fault/failure tolerance, software engineering, and mathematics – as employed across the communities and specialties – constitute the means to achieve the end objectives.77 The principles for trustworthy secure design are listed in Table 4.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 信頼できるセキュアな設計原則は、安全性、セキュリティ、信頼性、生存性、レジリエンスの各コミュニティ、およびそれらに関連する専門エンジニアリング分野の実務を代表するものである。これらの実務の目標を総合すると、有害な影響を信頼できる形で制御するためにシステムが満たすべき最終目的を構成する。原則は、信頼されたオペレーティングシステムへのメカニズムの早期組込みから、今日のコンポーネント、環境、システムに至るまでの研究、開発、適用の経験に根差しており、新たに登場し、発展し、成熟するアプローチにも今後も普遍的に適用できると期待される。コンピューター科学、コンピューター工学、システム工学、制御システム、故障・障害許容、ソフトウェア工学、数学の各分野の概念と定理は、各コミュニティおよび専門分野で活用され、最終目的を達成する手段となる。77 信頼できるセキュアな設計原則を表4に示す。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Principle: The rigor associated with the conduct of an engineering activity provides the confidence required to address the most significant adverse effect that can occur. Note: Rigor determines the scope, depth, and detail of an engineering activity. Rigor is a means of providing confidence in the results of a completed engineering activity. Generally, an increase in rigor translates to an increase in confidence in the results of the activity. Further, increased confidence reduces the uncertainty that can also reduce risk or provide a better understanding of what to address to achieve risk reduction. The relationship between rigor and the criticality of data and information used to make decisions is recognized by systems analysis practices [4]. The principle of commensurate rigor helps to ensure that the concept of rigor is included as an equal factor in the trade space of capability, adverse effect, cost, and schedule in the planning and conduct of engineering activities, method and tool selection, and personnel selection. An increase in rigor may translate into an increase in the cost of personnel, methods, and tools required to complete rigorous engineering activities or an increase in schedule to accomplish the activities with the expected rigor. Any increased cost that may occur can be justified by acquiring confidence about system performance to limit loss while also addressing the system’s ability to deliver the capability. Therefore, the rigor associated with an engineering activity should be commensurate with the significance of the most adverse effect associated with the activity. References: [2] [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 原則：エンジニアリング活動の実施に伴う厳密さは、発生し得る最も重大な悪影響に対処するために必要な確信をもたらす。注：厳密さは、エンジニアリング活動の範囲、深さ、詳細度を定める。厳密さは、完了したエンジニアリング活動の結果への確信をもたらす手段である。一般に、厳密さを高めると活動の結果への確信も高まる。さらに、確信の向上によって不確実性が低減し、リスクが低下するか、リスク低減のために何に対処すべきかをよりよく理解できる。意思決定に用いるデータと情報の重要度と厳密さの関係は、システム分析の実務で認識されている[4]。均衡した厳密さの原則は、エンジニアリング活動の計画・実施、手法・ツールの選択、人員の選定において、能力、悪影響、費用、日程のトレードオフ空間に厳密さを同等の要因として含めるのに役立つ。厳密さを高めるには、厳密なエンジニアリング活動を完了するために必要な人員、手法、ツールの費用増、または期待される厳密さで活動を完了するための日程延長が伴うことがある。発生し得る費用増は、システムが能力を提供する能力にも対処しながら、損失を限定するシステム性能への確信を得ることで正当化できる。したがって、エンジニアリング活動に伴う厳密さは、その活動に関連する最も重大な悪影響に見合うべきである。参考文献：[2] [4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: E.6. Commensurate Trustworthiness

page_check.proof_note: E.6. Commensurate Trustworthiness is a heading, listed as a paragraph.

rebuilt_blocks.html: Principle: A system element is trustworthy to a level commensurate with the most significant adverse effect that results from a failure of that element. Note: A trusted element continuously exhibits properties of trust during the time that it is depended upon by other system elements. The degree of trustworthiness needed for a trusted element is determined by those entities that depend on the element. Some basis is required to support decisions about trust and trustworthiness. The basis includes expressing the trust that is to be placed in a system element, expressing the trustworthiness that is exhibited by the element, and comparing the trustworthiness of different system elements. This principle is particularly relevant when considering systems and elements with complex chains of trust dependencies. References: [4] [20]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 原則：システム要素は、その要素の故障から生じる最も重大な悪影響に見合う水準で信頼できる。注：信頼された要素は、他のシステム要素から依存されている間、信頼の特性を継続的に示す。信頼された要素に必要な信頼性の度合いは、その要素に依存するエンティティによって決まる。信頼と信頼性に関する判断を裏付ける根拠が必要である。その根拠には、システム要素に置く信頼の表明、その要素が示す信頼性の表明、および異なるシステム要素の信頼性の比較が含まれる。この原則は、信頼依存関係が複雑に連鎖するシステムや要素を検討する際に特に重要である。参考文献：[4] [20]

page_check.proof_note: Joins the E.6 Principle, the Note and the References line into one block; separate paragraphs. The E.7 heading follows.

rebuilt_blocks.html: Principle: The system design is trustworthy for each aggregate composition of interacting system elements. Note: The trustworthiness of an aggregate of composed system elements cannot be assumed based on the trustworthiness assertions of each individual element in the aggregate. Further, the trustworthiness of an aggregate of composed trustworthy system elements cannot be assumed to be equal to the trustworthiness of the least trustworthy element in the aggregate. By definition, a system is a combination of interacting system elements. Each system function results from the emergent behavior of a composed set of system elements. Similarly, the trustworthiness of a composed set of system elements is an emergent property of the composition. Therefore, the trustworthiness of the composed set of system elements (i.e., aggregate) for a given system function must be determined by treating the aggregate as a single discrete element. The compositional trustworthiness principle addresses how an argument can be made for system-level trustworthiness given how the constituent elements of the system compose to form the system and do so by adhering to the composition principles. References: [2] [4] [36] [42]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 原則：システム設計は、相互作用するシステム要素を集約して合成するそれぞれの場合に、信頼できる。注：合成されたシステム要素の集合体の信頼性は、その集合体を構成する個々の要素の信頼性の主張から推定できない。さらに、信頼できるシステム要素を合成した集合体の信頼性が、その集合体で最も信頼性の低い要素の信頼性に等しいと推定することもできない。定義上、システムは相互作用するシステム要素の組合せである。各システム機能は、合成されたシステム要素群の創発的な振る舞いによって実現する。同様に、合成されたシステム要素群の信頼性は、その合成によって創発する特性である。したがって、特定のシステム機能に関する合成システム要素群（すなわち集合体）の信頼性は、その集合体を単一の個別要素として扱って判断しなければならない。合成による信頼性の原則は、システムの構成要素がどのように合成されてシステムを形成し、合成原則に従っているかを踏まえ、システムレベルの信頼性を論証する方法を扱う。参考文献：[2] [4] [36] [42]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Principle: Loss is prevented or minimized by employing multiple coordinated mechanisms. Note: The coordinated deployment of multiple protective mechanisms for a system helps to avoid single points of failure. The principle of defense in depth has three pillars: - Multiple lines of defenses or barriers should be placed along loss scenario sequences. - Loss control should not rely on a single defensive element. - The successive barriers should be diverse in nature and include technical, operational, and organizational barriers [52]. Defense in depth requires the use of coordinated mechanisms (active) within an architectural structure (passive) that achieves the depth characteristic.81 Ideally, the initial lines of defense prevent loss, while subsequent lines of defense block loss scenario escalation and/or contain loss and potential consequences when needed. A defense-in-depth strategy examines loss scenarios for those points of opportunity to prevent or contain loss. It also leverages the opportunities to use active or passive mechanisms or constraints to meet loss control objectives. The coordination of defense-in-depth mechanisms (i.e., combinations of structural, data, and control flow coordination) in conjunction with other design principles (e.g., Anomaly Detection, Commensurate Response) reflects a design strategy to satisfy the specified loss control objectives. While defense in depth distributes the protection capability to many components, a defense-in-depth strategy may also consider a distributed composition to a line of defense. A protection capability provided by a single system component is a potential single point of failure or bottleneck to system performance. It may also raise other concerns. A distributed composition of a defense layer may provide additional options within the coordination of layers. Defense in depth is, in part, a form of the principle of Protective Failure. It helps satisfy the objective that a failure of a system element should not result in an unacceptable loss. However, it does not satisfy the objective that a failure of a system element should not invoke another loss scenario. References: [2] [21] [40] [47]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 原則：複数の協調したメカニズムを用いて、損失を防止または最小化する。注：システムに複数の保護メカニズムを協調して配備すると、単一障害点を避けるのに役立つ。多層防御の原則には3つの柱がある：- 損失シナリオの連鎖に沿って、複数の防御線または障壁を配置すべきである。 - 損失制御を単一の防御要素に依存させるべきではない。 - 障壁は連続するものごとに性質を異にし、技術的、運用上、組織上の障壁を含めるべきである[52]。多層防御には、深層性という特性を実現するアーキテクチャ構造（受動的）内で、協調するメカニズム（能動的）を用いる必要がある。81 理想的には、最初の防御線が損失を防ぎ、後続の防御線が必要に応じて損失シナリオの拡大を阻止し、損失および潜在的な結果を封じ込める。多層防御戦略では、損失を防止または封じ込める機会となる箇所について損失シナリオを検討する。また、損失制御目的を満たすために、能動的または受動的なメカニズムや制約を利用する機会も活用する。多層防御メカニズム（すなわち、構造、データ、制御フローの調整の組合せ）を他の設計原則（例：異常検知、均衡した対応）と組み合わせて調整することは、指定された損失制御目的を満たす設計戦略を示す。多層防御は保護能力を多数のコンポーネントに分散させるが、防御線を分散合成することも戦略上検討できる。単一のシステムコンポーネントが提供する保護能力は、潜在的な単一障害点またはシステム性能のボトルネックである。また、他の懸念を生じさせることもある。防御層を分散合成すれば、各層の調整における選択肢を増やせる可能性がある。多層防御は、部分的には保護的な故障の原則の一形態である。システム要素の故障によって許容できない損失が生じてはならないという目的を満たすのに役立つ。ただし、システム要素の故障によって別の損失シナリオが誘発されてはならないという目的までは満たさない。参考文献：[2] [21] [40] [47]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Principle: Multiple authorized entities act in a coordinated manner before an operation on the system is allowed to occur. Note: Distributed privilege82 is a means to require agreement and coordination from multiple entities when performing an operation, thereby preventing a single entity from acting alone. Distributed privilege separates, divides, or in some other manner distributes the privileges required to perform an operation among multiple entities. This distribution includes a set of rules, conditions, and constraints that describe how multiple entities must interact through positive actions before a requested operation can proceed and be completed. The rules, conditions, and constraints may reflect combinations of the following: - Simultaneous Actions: Multiple different authorized entities execute a command within a specified time window. - Sequenced Actions: Multiple different entities interact within a linear sequence of actions where each successive action is enabled only by the successful completion of a prior action. - Parallel Actions: Multiple entities execute sequences concurrently, and success is achieved either by a consensus of the results of each concurrent action or by voting among the participants. Defeating distributed privilege requires collusion to take an unauthorized or improper action. In the case of an attack, distributed privilege forces the adversary to target all of the entities to whom privilege is distributed. References: [21] [46]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 原則：システム上の操作が許可される前に、複数の認可されたエンティティが協調して行動する。注：分散特権82は、操作の実行時に複数のエンティティ間の合意と協調を要求し、単一エンティティが単独で行動するのを防ぐ手段である。分散特権は、操作に必要な特権を複数のエンティティ間で分離、分割、またはその他の方法で分配する。この分配には、要求された操作を進行・完了させる前に、複数のエンティティが積極的な行動を通じてどのように相互作用しなければならないかを定める一連の規則、条件、制約が含まれる。規則、条件、制約には、次の組合せが反映されることがある：- 同時動作：複数の異なる認可済みエンティティが、指定された時間枠内にコマンドを実行する。 - 順序動作：複数の異なるエンティティが直線的な動作順序で相互作用し、後続の各動作は直前の動作が正常に完了した場合にのみ可能になる。 - 並列動作：複数のエンティティが一連の動作を同時並行に実行し、それぞれの動作結果の合意、または参加者間の投票によって成功を決定する。分散特権を破るには、認可されていない、または不適切な行動をとるための共謀が必要である。攻撃の場合、分散特権によって、敵対者は特権の分配先であるすべてのエンティティを標的にしなければならない。参考文献：[21] [46]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Principle: The system design delivers the required capability through structural, behavioral, or data or control flow variation. Note: A system design that incorporates diversity helps to avoid common mode failures and introduces unpredictability to adversaries, thus complicating the planning and execution of where, when, and how to target their attacks. While the system behaviors that result from a design may be unpredictable from the viewpoint of the adversary, the design itself must be predictable and verifiable in achieving only the intended outcomes. The options for diversity include variety in the system structural and architectural design elements, the system functional and behavioral elements, the interfaces and interconnections between interfaces, the data and control flow, and the technology and component selection. Diversity can reside in: - Fixed or static characteristics of the system (e.g., multiple instances of a system element, multiple communication channels)
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 原則：システム設計は、構造、振る舞い、データ、または制御フローの変化を通じて、必要な能力を提供する。注：多様性を取り入れたシステム設計は、共通原因故障を避けるのに役立ち、敵対者にとって予測不能性を高めるため、攻撃の対象、時期、方法の計画と実行を困難にする。設計から生じるシステムの振る舞いは敵対者の観点から予測不能であっても、設計自体は、意図した結果だけを実現する上で予測可能かつ検証可能でなければならない。多様性の選択肢には、システムの構造・アーキテクチャ設計要素、機能・振る舞い要素、インターフェースと相互接続、データ・制御フロー、技術・コンポーネント選択における多様性が含まれる。多様性は次に見られる：- システムの固定的または静的な特性（例：システム要素の複数インスタンス、複数の通信チャネル）

rebuilt_blocks.html: Top-level claims decompose in a structured manner into subclaims about the desired attributes of a trustworthy secure system. Subclaims address the requirements, design, implementation, methods, and adversities that demonstrate that the system adequately contributes to ensuring only authorized and intended system behaviors and outcomes. These subclaims are derived from concerns about the completeness and accuracy of stakeholder and system requirements,89 enforcement of the security policy, proper implementation of the design, proper maintenance of the system, the usability of the system,90 and the avoidance, minimization, and mitigation of defects, errors, and vulnerabilities.91 Other subclaims may exist involving the ability to exhibit predictable behavior while operating in secure states in the presence and absence of adversity and the ability to recover from an insecure state. Claims can be expressed in terms of functional correctness, strength of function, and the protection capability derived from adherence to standards and/or from the use of specific processes, procedures, and methods.

Due to associated costs and complexity, formal methods are typically limited to engineering efforts where only the highest levels of assurance are needed, such as the formal modeling, specification, and verification of security policy and the implementation that enforces the policy (Section D.4.2). rebuilt_blocks.html: concept of operations Verbal and graphic statement, in broad outline, of an organization’s assumptions or intent in regard to an operation or series of operations of new, modified, or existing organizational systems. [77] Note 1: The concept of operations is frequently embodied in long-range strategic plans and annual operational plans. In the latter case, the concept of operations in the plan covers a series of connected operations to be conducted simultaneously or in succession to achieve an organizational performance objective. Note 2: The concept of operations provides the basis for bounding the operating space, system capabilities, interfaces, and operating environment.

rebuilt_blocks.html: concept of secure function A strategy for the achievement of secure system function that embodies the preemptive and reactive protection capabilities of the system. Note 1: This strategy strives to prevent, minimize, or detect the events and conditions that can lead to the loss of an asset and the resultant adverse consequences; prevent, minimize, or detect the loss of an asset or adverse asset consequences; continuously deliver system capability at some acceptable level despite the impact of threats or uncertainty; and recover from adverse asset consequences to restore full system capability or recover to some acceptable level of system capability. Note 2: The concept of secure function is adapted from historical and other secure system concepts, such as the Philosophy of Protection, the Theory of Design and Operation, and the Theory of Compliance.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: concept of secure function（セキュア機能の概念） システムの予防的および事後対応的な保護能力を具現化する、セキュアなシステム機能を達成するための戦略。注1：この戦略は、次のことを目指す。資産の損失およびその結果として生じる有害な結果につながり得る事象や状態を防止、最小化、または検出すること。資産の損失または資産に対する有害な結果を防止、最小化、または検出すること。脅威または不確実性の影響があっても、許容可能な水準でシステム能力を継続的に提供すること。資産に対する有害な結果から回復して、システム能力を完全に復旧するか、許容可能な水準のシステム能力まで回復すること。注2：セキュア機能の概念は、保護の哲学、設計および運用の理論、適合性の理論など、従来の概念やその他のセキュアシステムの概念を応用したものである。

rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: risk 目的に対する不確実性の影響。[28]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note 1: An effect is a deviation from the expected, positive or negative. A positive effect is also known as an opportunity. Note 2: Objectives can have different aspects (i.e., financial, health and safety, and environmental goals) and can apply at different levels (i.e., strategic, organization-wide, project, product, and process). Note 3: Risk is often characterized by reference to potential events and consequences or a combination of these. Note 4: Risk is often expressed in terms of a combination of the consequences of an event (including changes in circumstances) and the associated likelihood of occurrence. Note 5: Uncertainty is the state, even partial, of deficiency of information related to the understanding or knowledge of an event, its consequence, or likelihood.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注1：影響とは、期待からの正または負の逸脱である。正の影響は機会とも呼ばれる。注2：目的には異なる側面（すなわち、財務、健康と安全、環境に関する目標）があり、異なるレベル（すなわち、戦略、組織全体、プロジェクト、製品、プロセス）に適用される場合がある。注3：リスクは、潜在的な事象と結果、またはそれらの組み合わせを参照して表されることが多い。注4：リスクは、事象の結果（状況の変化を含む）とその発生可能性の組み合わせで表現されることが多い。注5：不確実性とは、事象、その結果、または可能性の理解もしくは知識に関する情報が、部分的であっても不足している状態である。

rebuilt_blocks.html: risk analysis Process to comprehend the nature of risk and to determine the level of risk. [28]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: risk analysis リスクの性質を理解し、リスクの水準を決定するプロセス。[28]

rebuilt_blocks.html: risk assessment Overall process of risk identification, risk analysis, and risk evaluation. [28]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: risk assessment リスク特定、リスク分析、およびリスク評価から成る全体的なプロセス。[28]

rebuilt_blocks.html: risk criteria Terms of reference against which the significance of a risk is evaluated. [28] risk evaluation Process of comparing the results of risk analysis with risk criteria to determine whether the risk and/or its magnitude is/are acceptable or tolerable. [28]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: risk criteria リスクの重大性を評価するための参照条件。[28] risk evaluation リスクおよび／またはその大きさが受容可能または許容可能かどうかを判断するため、リスク分析の結果をリスク基準と比較するプロセス。[28]

page_check.proof_note: joins risk criteria (page 73) and risk evaluation (top of page 74), separate glossary entries; joins risk criteria (page 73) and risk evaluation; only risk evaluation is printed on page 74

rebuilt_blocks.html: risk identification Process of finding, recognizing, and describing risks. [28]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: risk identification リスクを発見し、認識し、記述するプロセス。[28]

rebuilt_blocks.html: risk management Coordinated activities to direct and control an organization with regard to risk. [28]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: risk management リスクに関して組織を指揮し、管理するための調整された活動。[28]

rebuilt_blocks.html: risk tolerance The organization or stakeholder’s readiness to bear the risk after risk treatment in order to achieve its objectives. [28]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: risk tolerance 目的を達成するため、リスク対応後のリスクを負う組織または利害関係者の意思。[28]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: Risk tolerance can be influenced by legal or regulatory requirements.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：リスク許容度は、法的または規制上の要件によって影響を受ける場合がある。

rebuilt_blocks.html: risk treatment Process to modify risk. [28]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: risk treatment リスクを変更するプロセス。[28]

rebuilt_blocks.html: safety Expectation that a system does not, under defined conditions, lead to a state in which human life, health, property, or the environment is endangered. [86]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: safety 定義された条件下で、システムが人命、健康、財産、または環境が危険にさらされる状態をもたらさないという期待。[86]

rebuilt_blocks.html: security Freedom from those conditions that can cause the loss of assets with unacceptable consequences.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security 受け入れられない結果を伴う資産損失を引き起こし得る状態からの自由。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security architecture A set of physical and logical security-relevant representations (i.e., views) of system architecture that conveys information about how the system is partitioned into security domains and makes use of security-relevant elements to enforce security policies within and between security domains based on how data and information must be protected.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security architecture システムがセキュリティドメインにどのように分割されるかを伝え、データおよび情報の保護要件に基づいて、セキュリティドメイン内およびドメイン間でセキュリティポリシーを実施するためにセキュリティ関連要素をどのように用いるかを示す、システムアーキテクチャの物理的および論理的なセキュリティ関連表現（すなわち、ビュー）の集合。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: The security architecture reflects security domains, the placement of security-relevant elements within the security domains, the interconnections and trust relationships between the security-relevant elements, and the behavior and interactions between the security-relevant elements. The security architecture, like the system architecture, may be expressed at various levels of abstraction and with different scopes.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：セキュリティアーキテクチャは、セキュリティドメイン、各ドメイン内のセキュリティ関連要素の配置、セキュリティ関連要素間の相互接続および信頼関係、ならびにそれらの要素間の振る舞いと相互作用を反映する。システムアーキテクチャと同様に、セキュリティアーキテクチャはさまざまな抽象化レベルおよび異なる範囲で表現できる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security design order of precedence A design approach for minimizing the design basis for loss potential and using architectural features to provide structure for implementing engineered security features and devices.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security design order of precedence 損失可能性の設計基盤を最小化し、設計されたセキュリティ機能および装置の実装構造を提供するためにアーキテクチャ上の特徴を用いる設計アプローチ。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security domain Set of assets and resources subject to a common security policy. [85]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security domain 共通のセキュリティポリシーの適用を受ける資産およびリソースの集合。[85]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: A security domain is defined by rules (policy) for users, processes, systems, and services that apply to activities within the domain and activities with similar entities in other domains.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：セキュリティドメインは、ドメイン内の活動、および他のドメインにある同種の実体との活動に適用される、利用者、プロセス、システム、およびサービスに関する規則（ポリシー）によって定義される。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security function The capability provided by the system or a system element. The capability may be expressed generally as a concept or specified precisely in requirements.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security function（セキュリティ機能） システムまたはシステム要素が提供する能力。その能力は、概念として一般的に表現することも、要件として正確に規定することもできる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security mechanism A device or method for achieving a security-relevant purpose.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security mechanism（セキュリティ機構） セキュリティ関連の目的を達成するための装置または方法。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security policy A set of rules that governs all aspects of security-relevant system and system element behavior. Note 1: System elements include technology, machine, and human elements.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security policy（セキュリティポリシー） セキュリティ関連のシステムおよびシステム要素の振る舞いのすべての側面を規定する規則の集合。注1：システム要素には、技術、機械、および人間の要素が含まれる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note 2: Rules can be stated at high levels of abstraction (e.g., an organizational policy that defines the acceptable behavior of employees in performing their mission and business functions) or at low levels of abstraction (e.g., an operating system policy that defines the acceptable behavior of executing processes and the use of resources by those processes).
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注2：規則は、抽象化の高いレベル（例えば、ミッションおよび事業機能の遂行において従業員に許容される振る舞いを定義する組織ポリシー）でも、抽象化の低いレベル（例えば、実行中のプロセスに許容される振る舞いと、それらのプロセスによるリソースの使用を定義するオペレーティングシステムポリシー）でも記述できる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security relevance The functions or constraints that are relied upon to directly or indirectly meet protection needs.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security relevance（セキュリティ関連性） 保護ニーズを直接的または間接的に満たすために依拠する機能または制約。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: The term security relevance has been used to differentiate the role of system functions that singularly or in combination exhibit behavior, produce an outcome, or provide a capability to enforce authorized and intended system behavior or outcomes.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：「セキュリティ関連性」という用語は、単独または組み合わせて振る舞いを示し、結果を生み出し、または認可され意図されたシステムの振る舞いもしくは結果を実施する能力を提供するシステム機能の役割を区別するために用いられている。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security requirement A requirement that has security relevance.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security requirement（セキュリティ要件） セキュリティ関連性を持つ要件。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security risk The effect of uncertainty on objectives pertaining to asset loss and the associated consequences. [28]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security risk（セキュリティリスク） 資産損失およびそれに伴う結果に関する目的に対する不確実性の影響。[28]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: [28] defines risk as the effect of uncertainty on objectives. Furthermore, risk can be either positive or negative.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：[28]では、リスクを目的に対する不確実性の影響と定義している。さらに、リスクは正の場合も負の場合もある。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security service A security capability or function provided by an entity.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security service（セキュリティサービス） 実体が提供するセキュリティ能力または機能。

rebuilt_blocks.html: security specification The requirements for the security-relevant portion of the system.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: security specification（セキュリティ仕様） システムのセキュリティ関連部分に関する要件。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: The security specification may be provided as a separate document or may be captured with a broader specification.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：セキュリティ仕様は独立した文書として提供することも、より広範な仕様に含めることもできる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: self-protection The protection provided by an entity to ensure its own correct behavior and function despite adversity.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: self-protection（自己防護） 逆境下でも正しい振る舞いと機能を確保するために、実体が自らに提供する保護。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: While an entity would ideally be able to provide all the self-protection necessary, in practice entities are limited in the extent that they can provide for their own protection without depending on one or more other entities.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：実体は理想的には必要な自己防護をすべて提供できるが、実際には、1つ以上の他の実体に依存せずに自らを保護できる範囲に限界がある。

rebuilt_blocks.html: service Performance of activities, work, or duties. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: service（サービス） 活動、作業、または職務の遂行。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note 1: A service is self-contained, coherent, discrete, and can be composed of other services. Note 2: A service is generally an intangible product.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注1：サービスは自己完結的で、一貫性があり、個別に識別でき、他のサービスから構成される場合がある。注2：サービスは一般に無形の製品である。

rebuilt_blocks.html: situational awareness Perception of elements in the system and/or environment and a comprehension of their meaning, which could include a projection of the future status of perceived elements and the uncertainty associated with that status. [87]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: situational awareness（状況認識） システムおよび／または環境内の要素の知覚と、その意味の理解。知覚した要素の将来の状態およびそれに伴う不確実性の予測を含む場合がある。[87]

rebuilt_blocks.html: specification An information item that identifies, in a complete, precise, verifiable manner, the requirements, design, behavior, or other expected characteristics of a system, service, or process. [128] See security specification.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: specification（仕様） システム、サービス、またはプロセスの要件、設計、振る舞い、またはその他の期待される特性を、完全、正確、かつ検証可能な形で明示する情報項目。[128] security specificationを参照。

rebuilt_blocks.html: stage Period within the life cycle of an entity that relates to the state of its description or realization. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: stage（段階） 実体の記述または実現の状態に関連する、実体のライフサイクル中の期間。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note 1: As used in this document, stages relate to major progress and achievement milestones of the entity throughout its life cycle. Note 2: Stages often overlap. stakeholder Individual or organization having a right, share, claim, or interest in a system or in its possession of characteristics that meet their needs and expectations. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注1：本書で用いる「段階」は、ライフサイクルを通じた実体の主要な進捗および達成のマイルストーンを指す。注2：段階は重複することが多い。stakeholder（利害関係者） システム、または自身のニーズや期待を満たす特性をシステムが備えることに対して、権利、持分、主張、または利害を持つ個人または組織。[4]

page_check.proof_note: joins the notes of stage with the stakeholder entry, which is printed on page 76; Notes 1-2 (stages, from the previous page) are run together with the separate glossary entry 'stakeholder' which begins on this page

rebuilt_blocks.html: stakeholder (system) Individual, team, organization, or classes thereof having an interest in a system. [71]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: stakeholder (system)（利害関係者［システム］） システムに利害を持つ個人、チーム、組織、またはそれらの類型。[71]

rebuilt_blocks.html: strength of function Criterion expressing the minimum efforts assumed necessary to defeat the specified security behavior of an implemented security function by directly attacking its underlying security mechanisms.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: strength of function（機能強度） 実装されたセキュリティ機能の特定されたセキュリティ振る舞いを、その基盤となるセキュリティ機構への直接攻撃によって破るために必要と想定される最小努力を表す基準。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note 1: Strength of function has a prerequisite that assumes that the underlying security mechanisms are correctly implemented. The concept of strength of function may be equally applied to services or other capability-based abstraction provided by security mechanisms. Note 2: The term robustness combines the concepts of assurance of correct implementation with strength of function to provide finer granularity in determining the trustworthiness of a system.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注1：機能強度は、基盤となるセキュリティ機構が正しく実装されていることを前提条件とする。機能強度の概念は、セキュリティ機構が提供するサービスまたはその他の能力ベースの抽象化にも同様に適用できる。注2：「堅牢性」という用語は、正しい実装に対する保証と機能強度の概念を組み合わせ、システムの信頼性を判断する際の粒度を高める。

rebuilt_blocks.html: susceptibility The inability to avoid adversity.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: susceptibility（被影響性） 逆境を回避できないこと。

rebuilt_blocks.html: supplier Organization or an individual that enters into an agreement with the acquirer for the supply of a product or service. [4] Note 1: Other terms commonly used for supplier are contractor, producer, seller, or vendor. Note 2: The acquirer and the supplier are sometimes part of the same organization.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: supplier（供給者） 製品またはサービスの供給について取得者と合意を締結する組織または個人。[4] 注1：供給者には、請負業者、生産者、販売者、またはベンダーなどの用語も一般に用いられる。注2：取得者と供給者が同一組織の一部である場合もある。

rebuilt_blocks.html: system An arrangement of parts or elements that together exhibit behavior or meaning that the individual constituents do not. Systems can be physical or conceptual, or a combination of both. [3] [4] Note 1: A system is sometimes considered as a product or as the services that it provides. Note 2: In practice, the interpretation of its meaning is frequently clarified by the use of an associative noun (e.g., aircraft system). Alternatively, the word “system” is substituted simply by a context-dependent synonym (e.g., aircraft), though this potentially obscures a system principles perspective. Note 3: A complete system includes all associated equipment, facilities, material, computer programs, services, firmware, technical documentation, and personnel required for operations and support to the degree necessary for self-sufficient use in its intended environment.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: system（システム） 個々の構成要素だけでは示さない振る舞いまたは意味を、全体として示す部品または要素の集合体。システムは物理的なもの、概念的なもの、またはその両方の組み合わせであり得る。[3] [4] 注1：システムは、製品として、またはそれが提供するサービスとして見なされる場合がある。注2：実務上、その意味の解釈は、修飾名詞（例えば、航空機システム）を用いることで明確にされることが多い。あるいは、「システム」という語を文脈依存の同義語（例えば、航空機）に単に置き換えることもあるが、そうするとシステム原則の視点が不明瞭になる可能性がある。注3：完全なシステムには、意図された環境で自立して使用するために必要な範囲で、運用および支援に必要なすべての関連する機器、施設、資材、コンピュータープログラム、サービス、ファームウェア、技術文書、および人員が含まれる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: system element Member of a set of elements that constitute a system. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: system element（システム要素） システムを構成する要素群の一員。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: A system element is a discrete part of a system that can be implemented to fulfill specified requirements.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：システム要素は、指定された要件を満たすために実装できる、システムの個別部分である。

rebuilt_blocks.html: system of interest System whose life cycle is under consideration. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: system of interest（対象システム） そのライフサイクルが検討対象となっているシステム。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: system of systems System of interest whose system elements are themselves systems; typically, these entail large-scale interdisciplinary problems with multiple, heterogeneous, distributed systems. [15] Set of systems or system elements that interact to provide a unique capability that none of the constituent systems can accomplish on its own. [88]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: system of systems（システム・オブ・システムズ） そのシステム要素自体がシステムである対象システム。通常、複数の異種分散システムを伴う大規模な学際的課題である。[15] 構成システムが単独では実現できない独自の能力を提供するために相互作用する、システムまたはシステム要素の集合。[88]

rebuilt_blocks.html: system context The specific system elements, boundaries, interconnections, interactions, and operational environment that define a system. system life cycle Period that begins when a system is conceived and ends when the system is no longer available for use. [24] See life cycle stages.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: system context（システムコンテキスト） システムを定義する特定のシステム要素、境界、相互接続、相互作用、および運用環境。system life cycle（システムライフサイクル） システムが構想されてから、使用できなくなるまでの期間。[24] life cycle stagesを参照。

page_check.proof_note: Joins the entry 'system context' (this page) with the separate entry 'system life cycle', which is printed on the next page; Joins 'system context' (end of previous page) with the separate entry 'system life cycle' (top of this page)

rebuilt_blocks.html: system security requirement System requirement that has security relevance. System security requirements define the protection capabilities provided by the system, the performance and behavioral characteristics exhibited by the system, and the evidence used to determine that the system security requirements have been satisfied. Note 1: Due to the complexity of system security, system security requirements have several types and purposes, including (1) structural security requirements that express the passive aspects of the protection capability provided by the system architecture and (2) functional security requirements that express the active aspects of the protection capability provided by the engineered features and devices (e.g., security mechanisms, inhibits, controls, safeguards, overrides, and countermeasures). Note 2: Each system security requirement is expressed in a manner that makes verification possible via analysis, observation, test, inspection, measurement, or other defined and achievable means.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: system security requirement（システムセキュリティ要件） セキュリティ関連性を持つシステム要件。システムセキュリティ要件は、システムが提供する保護能力、システムが示す性能および振る舞いの特性、ならびにシステムセキュリティ要件が満たされたと判断するために用いる証拠を定める。注1：システムセキュリティは複雑であるため、システムセキュリティ要件には複数の種類と目的がある。これには、(1) システムアーキテクチャが提供する保護能力の受動的側面を表す構造セキュリティ要件、および (2) 設計された機能や装置（例えば、セキュリティ機構、抑止機構、制御、セーフガード、オーバーライド、および対抗策）が提供する保護能力の能動的側面を表す機能セキュリティ要件が含まれる。注2：各システムセキュリティ要件は、分析、観察、試験、検査、測定、またはその他の定義済みで達成可能な手段によって検証できる形で表現される。

rebuilt_blocks.html: systems engineering A transdisciplinary and integrative approach to enable the successful realization, use, and retirement of engineered systems, using systems principles and concepts, and scientific, technological, and management methods. [3] Interdisciplinary approach governing the total technical and managerial effort required to transform a set of stakeholder needs, expectations, and constraints into a solution and to support that solution throughout its life. [24]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: systems engineering（システムズエンジニアリング） システム原則および概念ならびに科学的、技術的、および管理上の方法を用いて、設計システムの実現、使用、および廃止を成功させるための、分野横断的かつ統合的なアプローチ。[3] 利害関係者の一連のニーズ、期待、および制約をソリューションに変換し、そのソリューションをライフサイクル全体にわたって支援するために必要な、技術面および管理面の総合的な取り組みを統括する学際的なアプローチ。[24]

rebuilt_blocks.html: systems security engineer Individual who practices the discipline of systems security engineering, regardless of their formal title. Additionally, the term systems security engineer refers to multiple individuals who operate on the same team or cooperating teams.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: systems security engineer（システムセキュリティエンジニア） 正式な肩書にかかわらず、システムセキュリティエンジニアリングの専門分野を実践する個人。さらに、「システムセキュリティエンジニア」は、同じチームまたは協力するチームで活動する複数の個人を指す。

rebuilt_blocks.html: systems security engineering A transdisciplinary and integrative approach to enable the successful secure realization, use, and retirement of engineered systems using systems, security, and other principles and concepts, as well as scientific, technological, and management methods. Systems security engineering is a subdiscipline of systems engineering.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: systems security engineering（システムセキュリティエンジニアリング） システム、セキュリティ、およびその他の原則と概念に加え、科学的、技術的、および管理上の方法を用いて、設計システムのセキュアな実現、使用、および廃止を成功させるための、分野横断的かつ統合的なアプローチ。システムセキュリティエンジニアリングは、システムズエンジニアリングの下位分野である。

rebuilt_blocks.html: tampering An intentional but unauthorized act resulting in the modification of a system, components of systems, its intended behavior, or data. [89]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: tampering（改ざん） システム、システムの構成要素、その意図された振る舞い、またはデータを変更する、意図的だが認可されていない行為。[89]

rebuilt_blocks.html: task Required, recommended, or permissible action intended to contribute to the achievement of one or more outcomes of a process. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: task（タスク） プロセスの1つ以上の成果の達成に寄与することを意図した、必須、推奨、または許容される行動。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: threat Potential cause of unacceptable asset loss and the undesirable consequences or impact of such a loss.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: threat（脅威） 受け入れられない資産損失と、そのような損失がもたらす望ましくない結果または影響の潜在的な原因。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: The specific causes of asset loss can arise from a variety of conditions and events related to adversity, typically referred to as disruptions, hazards, or threats. Regardless of the specific term used, the basis of asset loss constitutes all forms of intentional, unintentional, accidental, incidental, misuse, abuse, error, weakness, defect, fault, and/or failure events and associated conditions.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：資産損失の具体的な原因は、逆境に関連するさまざまな状態や事象から生じる場合があり、通常、混乱、危険、または脅威と呼ばれる。用いる具体的な用語にかかわらず、資産損失の原因には、意図的、非意図的、偶発的、付随的、誤用、濫用、エラー、弱点、欠陥、故障、および／または障害のあらゆる形態の事象と関連状態が含まれる。

rebuilt_blocks.html: traceability Discernible association among two or more logical entities, such as requirements, system elements, verifications, or tasks. [90] traceability matrix A matrix that records the relationship between two or more products of the development process (e.g., a matrix that records the relationship between the requirements and the design of a given software component). [24]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: traceability（トレーサビリティ） 要件、システム要素、検証、またはタスクなど、2つ以上の論理的実体間の識別可能な関連。[90] traceability matrix（トレーサビリティマトリクス） 開発プロセスの2つ以上の成果物間の関係を記録するマトリクス（例えば、特定のソフトウェアコンポーネントの要件と設計の関係を記録するマトリクス）。[24]

rebuilt_blocks.html: trade-off Decision-making actions that select from various requirements and alternative solutions on the basis of net benefit to the stakeholders. [4]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: trade-off（トレードオフ） 利害関係者にとっての純便益に基づいて、複数の要件および代替ソリューションから選択する意思決定行為。[4]

rebuilt_blocks.html: trade-off analysis Determining the effect of decreasing one or more key factors and simultaneously increasing one or more other key factors in a decision, design, or project.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: trade-off analysis（トレードオフ分析） 意思決定、設計、またはプロジェクトにおいて、1つ以上の主要因を減少させると同時に、別の1つ以上の主要因を増加させることの影響を判断すること。

rebuilt_blocks.html: transdisciplinary Creating a unity of intellectual frameworks beyond the disciplinary perspectives. [135]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: transdisciplinary（分野横断的） 各専門分野の視点を超えて、知的枠組みの統一を生み出すこと。[135]

rebuilt_blocks.html: trust A belief that an entity meets certain expectations and therefore, can be relied upon. [39]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: trust（信頼） 実体が一定の期待を満たし、したがって依拠できるという信念。[39]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: The term belief implies that trust may be granted to an entity whether the entity is trustworthy or not.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：「信念」という語は、実体が信頼に値するかどうかにかかわらず、その実体に信頼が与えられる場合があることを含意する。

rebuilt_blocks.html: trust relationship An agreed upon relationship between two or more system elements that is governed by criteria for secure interaction, behavior, and outcomes relative to the protection of assets.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: trust relationship（信頼関係） 資産保護に関するセキュアな相互作用、振る舞い、および結果の基準によって規律される、2つ以上のシステム要素間で合意された関係。

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: This refers to trust relationships between system elements implemented by hardware, firmware, and software.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：これは、ハードウェア、ファームウェア、およびソフトウェアによって実装されたシステム要素間の信頼関係を指す。

rebuilt_blocks.html: trustworthiness Worthy of being trusted to fulfill whatever critical requirements may be needed for a particular component, subsystem, system, network, application, mission, enterprise, or other entity. [2]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: trustworthiness（信頼性） 特定のコンポーネント、サブシステム、システム、ネットワーク、アプリケーション、ミッション、エンタープライズ、またはその他の実体に必要とされる重要な要件を満たすものとして信頼に値すること。[2]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: From a security perspective, a trustworthy system meets specific security requirements in addition to meeting other critical requirements.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：セキュリティの観点では、信頼できるシステムは、他の重要な要件に加えて、特定のセキュリティ要件も満たす。

rebuilt_blocks.html: trustworthy The degree to which the behavior of a component is demonstrably compliant with its stated requirements.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: trustworthy（信頼できる） コンポーネントの振る舞いが、その明示された要件に適合していることを実証できる度合い。

rebuilt_blocks.html: user Individual or group that interacts with a system or benefits from a system during its utilization. [91]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: user（利用者） システムの使用中にシステムと相互作用する、またはシステムから便益を受ける個人または集団。[91]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: The role of user and the role of operator are sometimes vested, simultaneously or sequentially, in the same individual or organization.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：利用者の役割と運用者の役割は、同一の個人または組織が同時に、または順次に担う場合がある。

rebuilt_blocks.html: validation Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that the requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled. [78]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: validation（妥当性確認） 特定の意図された使用または適用に関する要件が満たされたことを、客観的証拠の提示によって確認すること。[78]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: A system is able to accomplish its intended use, goals, and objectives (i.e., meet stakeholder requirements) in the intended operational environment. The right system was built.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：システムは、意図された運用環境において、意図された用途、目標、および目的を達成できる（すなわち、利害関係者要件を満たす）。正しいシステムを構築した。

rebuilt_blocks.html: verification Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that specified requirements have been fulfilled. [78]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: verification（検証） 指定された要件が満たされたことを、客観的証拠の提示によって確認すること。[78]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: Verification is a set of activities that compares a system or system element with the required characteristics. This includes but is not limited to specified requirements, design description, and the system itself. The system was built correctly.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：検証は、システムまたはシステム要素を必要な特性と比較する一連の活動である。これには、指定要件、設計記述、およびシステム自体が含まれるが、それらに限定されない。システムを正しく構築した。

rebuilt_blocks.html: view Representation of a whole system from the perspective of a related set of concerns. [92]
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: view（ビュー） 関連する一連の懸念事項の視点から見たシステム全体の表現。[92]

rebuilt_blocks.html: Note: A view can cover the entire system being examined or only a part of that system.
rebuilt_blocks.html_ja: 注：ビューは、検討対象のシステム全体を扱う場合も、その一部のみを扱う場合もある。

While defense in depth distributes the protection capability to many components, a defense-in-depth strategy may also consider a distributed composition to a line of defense. A protection capability provided by a single system component is a potential single point of failure or bottleneck to system performance. It may also raise other concerns. A distributed composition of a defense layer may provide additional options within the coordination of layers.

79 Battleshort is the capability to bypass normal interlocks in mission-critical equipment (e.g., equipment that must not be shut down or the mission function will fail) during battle conditions [51].
original_blocks.html_ja: 79 Battleshortとは、戦闘状況下で、任務遂行上重要な機器（例：停止すると任務機能が失敗するため停止してはならない機器）の通常のインターロックを迂回する能力である[51]。

original_blocks.html: Defense in depth is, in part, a form of the principle of Protective Failure. It helps satisfy the objective that a failure of a system element should not result in an unacceptable loss. However, it does not satisfy the objective that a failure of a system element should not invoke another loss scenario.

original_blocks.html: system of systems — System of interest whose system elements are themselves systems; typically, these entail large-scale interdisciplinary problems with multiple, heterogeneous, distributed systems. [15]
Set of systems or system elements that interact to provide a unique capability that none of the constituent systems can accomplish on its own. [88]

systems engineering — A transdisciplinary and integrative approach to enable the successful realization, use, and retirement of engineered systems, using systems principles and concepts, and scientific, technological, and management methods. [3]

Interdisciplinary approach governing the total technical and managerial effort required to transform a set of stakeholder needs, expectations, and constraints into a solution and to support that solution throughout its life. [24]

Security-dedicated or security-purposed system: The engineering effort delivers a system that satisfies a security-dedicated need or provides a security-oriented purpose and does so as a stand-alone system that may monitor or interact with other systems. Such systems can include surveillance systems, physical protection systems, monitoring systems, and security service provisioning systems.

High-confidence, dedicated-purpose system: The engineering effort delivers a system that satisfies the need for real-time vehicular control, industrial or utility processes, weapons, nuclear power plants, and other special-purpose needs. Such systems may include multiple operational states or modes with varying forms of manual, semi-manual, automated, or autonomous modes. These systems have highly deterministic properties, strict timing constraints, functional interlocks, and severe or catastrophic consequences of failure.

abstraction — View of an object that focuses on the information relevant to a particular purpose and ignores the remainder of the information. [24]
acquirer — Stakeholder that acquires or procures a product or service from a supplier. [4]
acquisition — Process of obtaining a system, product, or service. [4]
activity — Set of cohesive tasks of a process. [4]

adequate security (systems) — Meets minimum tolerable levels of security as determined by analysis, experience, or a combination of both and is as secure as reasonably practicable (i.e., incremental improvement in security would require an intolerable or disproportionate deterioration of meeting other system objectives, such as those for system performance, or would violate system constraints).
adverse consequence — An undesirable consequence associated with a loss. [61]
adversity — The conditions that can cause a loss of assets (e.g., threats, attacks, vulnerabilities, hazards, disruptions, and exposures).
agreement — Mutual acknowledgement of terms and conditions under which a working relationship is conducted (e.g., memorandum of agreement or contract). [4]
anomaly — Condition that deviates from expectations based on requirements specifications, design documents, user documents, or standards, or from someone’s perceptions or experiences. [24]

anti-tamper — Systems engineering activities intended to prevent or delay exploitation of critical program information in U.S. defense systems in domestic and export configurations to impede countermeasure development, unintended technology transfer, or alteration of a system due to reverse engineering. [70] See tampering.

architecture — Fundamental concepts or properties related to a system in its environment embodied in its elements, relationships, and in the principles of its design and evolution. [71] See security architecture.
architecture (system) — Fundamental concepts or properties of a system in its environment embodied in its elements, relationships, and in the principles of its design and evolution. [71]
architecture description — A work product used to express an architecture. [71]
architecture framework — Conventions, principles, and practices for the description of architectures established within a specific domain of application and/or community of stakeholders. [71]

original_blocks.html: architecture viewpoint — A work product establishing the conventions for the construction, interpretation, and use of architecture views to frame specific system concerns. [71]
artifact — Work products that are produced and used during a project to capture and convey information (e.g., models, source code). [72]
aspect — The parts, features, and characteristics used to describe, consider, interpret, or assess something.
asset — Anything that has value to a person or organization. [24]

Note 1: Assets have interrelated characteristics that include value, criticality, and the degree to which they are relied upon to achieve organizational mission and business objectives. From these characteristics, appropriate protections are to be engineered into solutions employed by the organization.

Note 2: An asset may be tangible (e.g., physical item such as hardware, software, firmware, computing platform, network device, or other technology components) or intangible (e.g., information, data, trademark, copyright, patent, intellectual property, image, or reputation).
assurance — Grounds for justified confidence that a claim has been or will be achieved. [61]

Note 1: Assurance is typically obtained relative to a set of specific claims. The scope and focus of such claims may vary (e.g., security claims, safety claims), and the claims themselves may be interrelated.
Note 2: Assurance is obtained through techniques and methods that generate credible evidence to substantiate claims.

assurance case — A reasoned, auditable artifact created that supports the contention that its top-level claim (or set of claims) is satisfied, including systematic argumentation and its underlying evidence and explicit assumptions that support the claim(s). [61]
assurance evidence — The information upon which decisions regarding assurance, trustworthiness, and risk of the solution are substantiated.

Note: Assurance evidence is specific to an agreed-upon set of claims. The security perspective focuses on assurance evidence for security-relevant claims, whereas other engineering disciplines may have their own focus (e.g., safety).
availability — Property of being accessible and usable on demand by an authorized entity. [73]
baseline — Formally approved version of a configuration item, regardless of media, formally designated and fixed at a specific time during the configuration item’s life cycle. [74]

Note: The engineering process generates many artifacts that are maintained as a baseline over the course of the engineering effort and after its completion. The configuration control processes of the engineering effort manage baselined artifacts. Examples include stakeholder requirements baseline, system requirements baseline, architecture/design baseline, and configuration baseline.
behavior — The way that an entity functions as an action, reaction, or interaction. How a system element, system, or system of systems acts, reacts, and interacts. [75]
body of evidence — The totality of evidence used to substantiate trust, trustworthiness, and risk relative to the system.
breakdown structure — Framework for efficiently controlling some aspect of the activities for a program or project. [76]

Note: Examples include work breakdown structure, the decomposition of the defined scope of a project into progressively lower levels consisting of elements of work, and product breakdown structure (i.e., decomposition of a product into its components).

claim — A true-false statement about the limitations on the values of an unambiguously defined property called the claim’s property; and limitations on the uncertainty of the property’s values falling within these limitations during the claim’s duration of applicability under stated conditions. [61]

complex system — A system in which there are non-trivial relationships between cause and effect: each effect may be due to multiple causes; each cause may contribute to multiple effects; causes and effects may be related as feedback loops, both positive and negative; and cause-effect chains are cyclic and highly entangled rather than linear and separable. [3]

concept of operations — Verbal and graphic statement, in broad outline, of an organization’s assumptions or intent in regard to an operation or series of operations of new, modified, or existing organizational systems. [77]

Note 1: The concept of operations is frequently embodied in long-range strategic plans and annual operational plans. In the latter case, the concept of operations in the plan covers a series of connected operations to be conducted simultaneously or in succession to achieve an organizational performance objective.
Note 2: The concept of operations provides the basis for bounding the operating space, system capabilities, interfaces, and operating environment.
concept of secure function — A strategy for the achievement of secure system function that embodies the preemptive and reactive protection capabilities of the system.

Note 1: This strategy strives to prevent, minimize, or detect the events and conditions that can lead to the loss of an asset and the resultant adverse consequences; prevent, minimize, or detect the loss of an asset or adverse asset consequences; continuously deliver system capability at some acceptable level despite the impact of threats or uncertainty; and recover from adverse asset consequences to restore full system capability or recover to some acceptable level of system capability.

Note 2: The concept of secure function is adapted from historical and other secure system concepts, such as the Philosophy of Protection, the Theory of Design and Operation, and the Theory of Compliance.
concern — Matter of interest or importance to a stakeholder. [71]
concern (system) — Interest in a system relevant to one or more of its stakeholders. [71]

original_blocks.html: configuration item — Item or aggregation of hardware, software, or both that is designated for configuration management and treated as a single entity in the configuration management process. [4]

original_blocks.html: consequence — Effect (change or non-change), usually associated with an event or condition or with the system and usually allowed, facilitated, caused, prevented, changed, or contributed to by the event, condition, or system. [61]

constraints — Limitation on the system, its design, its implementation, or the process used to develop or modify a system. Limitation that restricts the design solution, implementation, or execution of the system. [31]
Note: A constraint is a factor that is imposed on the solution by force or compulsion and may limit or modify the design.
control — Purposeful action on or within a process to meet specified objectives. The mechanism that achieves the action.
criticality — Degree of impact that a requirement, module, error, fault, failure, or other item has on the development or operation of a system.
customer — Organization or person that receives a product. [78]

cyber-physical system — A system integrating computation with physical processes whose behavior is defined by both the computational (digital and other forms) and the physical parts of the system. [27]

data — Representation of facts, concepts, or instructions in a manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing by humans or by automatic means. Collection of values assigned to base measures, derived measures, and/or indicators. [79]
derived requirement — A requirement deduced or inferred from the collection and organization of requirements into a particular system configuration and solution. [31]
Note 1: The next higher-level requirement is referred to as a parent requirement, while the derived requirement from this parent is called a child requirement.
Note 2: A derived requirement is typically identified during the elicitation of stakeholder requirements, requirements analysis, trade studies or validation.

design — Process to define the architecture, system elements, interfaces, and other characteristics of a system or system element. [24] Result of the process to be consistent with the selected architecture, system elements, interfaces, and other characteristics of a system or system element. [4]
